B: Hello! Matthew? Hi!
A: Hi, yeah, hi. Sorry, it took a second to connect. Hi. Matthew, I'm in Norwich.
B: Marisol, Leyton, East London. Norwich, very nice, I've never been. Is it far from the sea?
A: Not too far. I grew up in Lowestoft actually, right on the coast, so I drive back most fortnights. My dad had a knee operation, so, erm, a bit more often at the moment.
B: Ay, knees. My husband says his knees are finished every morning and he's fifty. How is your dad?
A: Getting there. He's a terrible patient. Won't do his exercises, then complains it hurts.
B: Men! Sorry, sorry, not you. What do you do, Matthew?
A: Erm, I'm a flood risk modeller. So basically computer models of rivers, really. If someone wants to build near a river, I work out where the water goes if it floods. Then I try and explain it without everyone glazing over.
B: No, but that's important! I walk on Walthamstow Marshes, by the River Lea, and sometimes in winter it's like a lake. Is that normal or is that bad?
A: Ha, that's sort of the point of a marsh, actually. The water's meant to go there, so it's not going in people's houses. That's honestly the best version of flooding, the bit you can see on a walk.
B: Oh! So the marsh is working. I thought somebody forgot to fix something.
A: No, no, the marsh is doing its job. Probably better than most of us.
B: Ha! Better than my new lad at work, definitely. I manage a shop, convenience store in Walthamstow, twenty-two staff. He is lovely but late every day.
A: Twenty-two people, that's a lot. I'd be terrified. I sort of worry about managing even one person.
B: You get used to it. You learn their kids' names, who needs Saturdays off, who is crying in the stockroom because of a boyfriend. It's like a big family, a bit loud.
A: That sounds nice, actually. My office is very quiet. Everyone's got headphones on.
B: Too quiet! So who did you talk to already? I had Dean, from Kent, and Leanne.
A: Oh, I had Leanne first. She was lovely. We ended up talking about crying at Coco.
B: Leanne cried with me too! About our mums. She is a very good person, I think.
A: Yeah, she really is. She made me tell her what I'm having for dinner. Which is chilli, again, because I made a massive pan.
B: You must freeze it! Small boxes. You put the date on.
A: I know, I know. I always mean to.
B: Bueno, next time. At the weekend I cook Colombian, sancocho, a big soup, for my sister and friends. Ten, twelve people.
A: That sounds brilliant. I'd struggle to get twelve people in my flat. Or twelve chairs, honestly.
B: Ha, we sit on the stairs, on the bike in the spare room, anywhere!
A: On the exercise bike? While eating soup?
B: It's the only thing it's used for, I promise you. So you live on your own?
A: Yeah. One-bed. I'd like a cat but the lease says no. Sorry, is that
